clue.text: Livingstone conceals desire to take Cook's place

indicators.note: the former London mayor's name hides the urge inside itself, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: Ken Livingstone, a former Mayor of London
an itch is a restless longing for something

explanation.surface: A politician hides his ambition to replace a chef.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Livingstone was Mayor of London; his first name is wanted, not the explorer David Livingstone.
explanation.definitionFit: The room where a cook works and prepares meals is the kitchen.

clue.text: Stop Biko's representation on shilling

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first part above the second
a new representation of the name rearranges its letters

parts.note: the name of Steve Biko, the South African activist
sh is an old abbreviation for shilling, a former British coin

explanation.surface: Halt the depiction of Steve Biko on a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, abbreviated sh as well as s.
explanation.definitionFit: To kibosh something, or put the kibosh on it, is to halt or squash it.

clue.text: Donald and Ivana were once playing cards

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the married couple Donald and Ivana Trump
second meaning: cards of the suit that outranks the others

explanation.walkthrough: 'were once' points to their marriage, which ended in divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: The couple shared a surname, and in card games the winning suit's cards are called by the same word.

clue.text: Tough party punishment

parts.note: hard means difficult or tough
Labour is a major British political party

explanation.surface: A political party faces a harsh penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard labour was a prison sentence of heavy physical work imposed as a penalty.

clue.text: City rate's a young and beautiful maiden

parts.note: NY is New York
mph, miles per hour, is a rate of speed

explanation.surface: A city ranks a young woman as a beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth a nymph is a lovely young female spirit, hence any beautiful girl.

clue.text: Journalist envisaged "something with teeth"?

parts.note: hack is slang for a jobbing reporter
to have seen something in the mind's eye, past tense of see

explanation.surface: A reporter imagined some creature with fangs.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw for cutting metal has a toothed blade, so it is a tool with teeth.

clue.text: The Blairs' spin doctor?

indicators.note: spinning the letters round puts them in a new order

parts.note: the clue words themselves, Tony and Cherie's surname with the article, supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A media aide to Tony and Cherie Blair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin doctor' reads as one phrase, a press manager; split it, and spin is the anagram signal and doctor the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbalist treats illness with plant remedies, so is a kind of healer.

clue.text: Irritating little beast gains Conservative support

parts.note: a leg holds up a table or chair

explanation.surface: An annoying creature wins the backing of a Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleg is a horsefly, a biting insect that pesters animals and people.

clue.text: Illegal traveller in Cotswold town on holiday

parts.note: Stow-on-the-Wold, a market town in the Cotswold hills of England
away from home on a break

explanation.surface: An unlawful passenger is found in an English country town during a vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: A stowaway hides aboard a ship or plane to travel without paying.

clue.text: Newspapers reporting tenuous stories

indicators.note: reporting is speech, so the phrase is taken by its spoken sound

parts.note: weak lies, flimsy untruths

explanation.surface: Papers publish flimsy articles.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeklies are periodicals issued once every seven days.

clue.text: More colourful look to Sky — and stronger!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sky of a deeper blue hue
second meaning: of language, more risqué or obscene

explanation.walkthrough: Blue language is coarse, so stronger language is the comparative of that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of the colour word also serves for cruder, more explicit talk or jokes.

clue.text: Detective's set of rules for transmission system?

parts.note: Inspector Morse, the Oxford detective of novels and television
a code is a body of regulations

explanation.surface: An inspector's rulebook turns out to be a gearbox design.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is Colin Dexter's fictional Oxford policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: The dots-and-dashes scheme invented by Samuel Morse for telegraph signalling is a way of sending messages.

clue.text: Call pusher sad and gloomy

indicators.note: something in a sad, sorry state is in poor order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the two clue words, phone a drug dealer on the surface, supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Phoning a drug dealer leaves one miserable and depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sad' looks like part of the definition beside 'gloomy', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepulchral means tomb-like, hence dismal and funereal in mood.

clue.text: Marine beast's audible cry

indicators.note: audible means as heard, so the sea creature's name is taken for its sound

parts.note: a whale is a large sea mammal

explanation.surface: The call of a sea creature can be heard far off.
explanation.definitionFit: A wail is a long, high mournful cry or howl.

clue.text: Great things smell good in restaurants

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell

indicators.note: places the letter for good within the eateries

parts.note: diners are roadside eating places

explanation.surface: Fine food aromas fill the eating places.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a hum is a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: A humdinger is an informal word for something remarkable or outstanding.

clue.text: Get a downer on ambiguous Arab tribute

indicators.note: something ambiguous can be read in different ways, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the two clue words, a gift to an Arab on the surface, supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Feeling low about an unclear gift to an Arab.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbiturate is a sedative drug, and depressants are called downers in slang.

clue.text: Reformation of IRA marred by gatecrasher?

indicators.note: reforming something gives it a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the clue words, the paramilitary group spoiled on the surface, supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A reformed paramilitary group, spoiled by an intruder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gatecrasher' is literal here: a ram-raider drives a vehicle through a shop front to loot it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ram raider literally crashes a car through gates or windows to break in.

clue.text: Frigid bags only want diamonds — loads!

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
packs are bundles carried as loads

explanation.surface: Cold-hearted gold-diggers want nothing but jewels, and plenty of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice packs are pouches of frozen material used to cool injuries.

clue.text: Agitate for world council pay

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations
to settle a bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: Campaign for the global body to cover the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle is to disturb or make anxious.

clue.text: Against smut made about "completed" marriage

parts.note: con, as in pros and cons, means an argument against

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so these letters are shuffled into a new order

parts.note: the two clue words, dirty talk produced on the surface, supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone objects to dirty talk surrounding a wedding night.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage is consummated when it is made complete by sexual union, so completed is the sense.

clue.text: Palace and cathedral on bishop's patch

indicators.note: in a down clue, the cathedral sits on top of the diocese

parts.note: Ely is an English cathedral city
a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A palace and a cathedral stand in a bishop's diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: The Élysée Palace in Paris is the French president's residence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Élysée is the Paris palace that serves as the official home of France's president.

clue.text: Club worker and literary hero

parts.note: a bat is a club for hitting a ball
a man is an employee or hand

explanation.surface: A golf-club employee who is also a fictional champion.
explanation.walkthrough: A batman is also an army officer's servant, so 'Club worker' reads as a second meaning too.
explanation.definitionFit: Batman is the caped superhero of DC comic books, a fictional crime-fighter.

clue.text: Vulgar person (the Parisian) in the lead

indicators.note: in places the French article within the symbol for lead

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A coarse type gets to the front, perhaps in a Paris race.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleb, short for plebeian, is a dismissive word for a common or uncouth person.

clue.text: We hear Rushdie and Fitzgerald, perhaps, are cause of ill feeling

indicators.note: we hear tells us the two first names are to be taken for how they sound together

parts.note: the writer Salman Rushdie and the singer Ella Fitzgerald

explanation.surface: Gossip that a novelist and a jazz singer have upset someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' flags that these are examples of people with those first names.
explanation.definitionFit: Salmonella bacteria bring on food poisoning, which makes people feel ill.

clue.text: Soldier wearing raincoat for a spell

indicators.note: the soldier wears the coat, so goes inside it

parts.note: mac, short for mackintosh, a British word for a raincoat
GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier in a waterproof waits out a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' looks like a period of time, but it is a charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic is sorcery, and a spell is an act of enchantment.

clue.text: Fixes up operation for privates?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pins fasten or fix things

explanation.surface: An army surgeon patches up the rank and file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'privates' looks like soldiers, but means the genitals: a snip is a vasectomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Snip is slang for a vasectomy, a minor surgical procedure on the male genitals.

clue.text: Like domestic animals quarrelling savagely

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as two household pets are
second meaning: fighting like ..., bitterly and constantly

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'fight like cat and dog' supplies the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The two commonest household pets are proverbial for bitter, endless fighting.

clue.text: Course record set outside Munich, initially

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records, so a set of them

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words, taken by the initially signal

explanation.surface: A new best time is achieved beyond a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: EPSOM is a racecourse in Surrey, home of the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs is a famous English horse-racing track, so it is a racecourse.

clue.text: Coach for retiring rail supporter?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a railway carriage with beds for those going to bed
second meaning: a beam laid across the track beneath the rails

explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a trainer and 'retiring' like giving up work, but it is a train car for going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a night-train berth carriage and a wooden or concrete track tie are called by this word.

clue.text: Curie's firm builds a tank

parts.note: Ci is the symbol for the curie, the unit of radioactivity named after Marie Curie
stern means strict or unyielding

explanation.surface: A scientist's company constructs an armoured vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company, but it is the adjective meaning strict.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is a water storage tank, as above a lavatory.
